campaign_name: Manhattan Bridge — material and arrangement evidence
purpose: Close the open questions that documents cannot. This model reaches 74 passing tests, and the open questions that survive are not all dimensional. Three of them are precisely what a photograph settles. OQ-019 records that materials are unregistered for the anchorages, the caissons, the cables, the stiffening trusses and both roadway surfaces -- every one of those is a question about what a thing is MADE OF. OQ-020 records that the approach viaducts' structural form is unregistered: girder type, pier form, bent arrangement. OQ-017 asks which way the Warren truss diagonals run at each panel and how the tower bracing is arranged. No amount of re-reading the 1909 Annual Report answers any of these; a person looking at an openly-licensed photograph answers all three. The dimensional questions -- OQ-001 cable sag, OQ-007 tower plan, OQ-024 anchorage arch springing -- are deliberately NOT in this campaign's category vocabulary, because a photograph without scale control in the frame cannot measure and must not be allowed to appear to.

area.note: Roughly the main-span midpoint. A 1.4 km radius reaches both towers, both anchorages and a useful part of both approaches. This coordinate is for SEARCH ONLY and is not a control. OQ-009 records that the real-world azimuth and geodetic anchor of the bridge axis are still provisional (grade D, DOQ-001), and a search centre must never quietly become the answer to that.

categories.label: masonry
categories.help: Anchorage and pier stonework close enough to tell the stone and see the coursing. MAT-010 was promoted to B on photographic evidence of dressed coursed ashlar; the anchorage arch barrel (MAT-022) rests on the same kind of reading. Feeds OQ-019.

categories.label: arch
categories.help: The anchorage thoroughfare arch and the tower arch openings. OQ-023 and OQ-024: these are modelled from a photograph rather than a dimension, so more photographs can confirm the FORM even though none of them may set the springing height.

categories.label: truss
categories.help: A transverse or oblique view of the stiffening trusses. OQ-017: the diagonal direction at each panel and the member sections are unregistered, and the web is currently drawn as lines rather than members (OQ-021). A photograph cannot measure a chord, but it can show which way the diagonals lean.

categories.label: cable
categories.help: Main cables, suspenders and cable bands. OQ-019 lists the cables among the unregistered materials; CONF-001 is an unresolved conflict over cable diameter that a photograph cannot settle but can at least illustrate.

categories.label: approach
categories.help: The approach viaducts from below or beside. OQ-020: the structural form is unregistered -- the model draws placeholder bents, and SRC-024 suggests a deck truss. This is the category that settles what actually carries the approaches.

categories.label: deck
categories.help: Roadway surfaces and their framing. OQ-019 names both roadway surfaces as unregistered materials.

categories.label: rail
categories.help: The four subway tracks on the lower deck and their supporting structure. OQ-010: the exact transverse centrelines are unregistered. A photograph shows the arrangement and the track structure without measuring the gauge separation.

categories.label: portal
categories.help: The Manhattan approach portal and its ornament. Modelled from very little; anything showing what is actually there is useful.

categories.label: context
categories.help: A good overall view that shows the bridge in its setting but settles no single component. Useful for the presentation layer, weak as evidence.

temporal_note: A 'renewed' subject is replaced on a maintenance cycle, so a photograph of it describes only the day it was taken. A 'stable' subject is substantially original fabric, so an archival frame is still evidence about it. Without the distinction a 1909 construction photograph could silently justify a claim about today's roadway or today's track structure.
